moon.name: Apollo 11
moon.crew: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked here; Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit.
moon.text: The Eagle lunar module landed on 20 July 1969. Armstrong and Aldrin spent about 21 hours on the surface, including a 2-hour 31-minute walk, and collected 21.6 kg of lunar material.

moon.name: Apollo 12
moon.crew: Pete Conrad and Alan Bean walked here; Richard Gordon remained in orbit.
moon.text: Landed on 19 November 1969, within walking distance of the Surveyor 3 lander, which had arrived in 1967. Two walks; 34.4 kg of samples.

moon.name: Apollo 14
moon.crew: Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell walked here; Stuart Roosa remained in orbit.
moon.text: Landed on 5 February 1971 at Fra Mauro, the original target of Apollo 13. Two walks; 42.3 kg of samples.

moon.name: Apollo 15
moon.crew: David Scott and James Irwin walked here; Alfred Worden remained in orbit.
moon.text: Landed on 30 July 1971 and used a lunar rover. Three walks; 76.8 kg of samples, including the Genesis Rock.

moon.name: Apollo 16
moon.crew: John Young and Charles Duke walked here; Ken Mattingly remained in orbit.
moon.text: Landed on 21 April 1972 in the lunar highlands. Three walks with a rover; 95.7 kg of samples.

moon.name: Apollo 17
moon.crew: Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt walked here; Ronald Evans remained in orbit.
moon.text: Landed on 11 December 1972. The most recent crewed landing, and the only one with a professional geologist on the surface (Schmitt). Three walks; 110.5 kg of samples.

moon.name: Luna 2
moon.text: Impacted the Moon on 13 September 1959. The earliest human-made object to reach the lunar surface.

moon.name: Luna 9
moon.text: A soft landing on 3 February 1966. Returned the earliest photographs from the lunar surface.

moon.name: Luna 13
moon.text: Soft landing on 24 December 1966. Returned panoramas and measured soil properties.

moon.name: Luna 16
moon.text: Soft landing on 20 September 1970. Returned 101 grams of lunar soil to Earth.

moon.name: Luna 17 / Lunokhod 1
moon.text: Landed on 17 November 1970 and deployed Lunokhod 1, which roved for about 10 months.

moon.name: Luna 20
moon.text: Landed on 21 February 1972 and returned 55 grams of highland soil.

moon.name: Luna 21 / Lunokhod 2
moon.text: Landed on 15 January 1973 and deployed Lunokhod 2, which travelled about 39 km.

moon.name: Luna 24
moon.text: Landed on 18 August 1976 and returned 170 grams of soil from Mare Crisium.

moon.name: Chang'e 3
moon.text: Soft landing on 14 December 2013, with the Yutu rover.

moon.name: Chang'e 4
moon.place: Von Kármán crater, South Pole–Aitken basin (far side)
moon.text: Landed on the far side on 3 January 2019, with the Yutu-2 rover, relayed through the Queqiao satellite.

moon.name: Chang'e 5
moon.text: Landed on 1 December 2020 and returned about 1.73 kg of samples to Earth.

moon.name: Chang'e 6
moon.place: Apollo basin, South Pole–Aitken, far side
moon.text: Landed on the far side on 1 June 2024 and returned about 1.89 kg of samples.

moon.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram)
moon.place: Near 69°S, between Manzinus C and Boguslawsky
moon.text: The Vikram lander reached the surface on 23 August 2023 and deployed the Pragyan rover.

moon.name: SLIM
moon.text: The Smart Lander for Investigating Moon reached the surface on 19 January 2024. It settled at a tilt but later returned images and spectroscopy.

moon.name: IM-1 Odysseus
moon.place: Malapert A, near the south pole
moon.text: Landed on 22 February 2024. The lander came to rest at a tilt and operated for several days near the south pole.

mars.name: Viking 1
mars.text: Landed on 20 July 1976. Operated on the surface until 1982, returning the long-running early record of Martian weather and panoramas.

mars.name: Viking 2
mars.text: Landed on 3 September 1976 in Utopia Planitia. The lander operated until 1980.

mars.name: Mars Pathfinder / Sojourner
mars.text: Landed on 4 July 1997 on airbags and deployed Sojourner, a small rover that travelled about 100 metres.

mars.name: Spirit (MER-A)
mars.text: Landed on 4 January 2004. The rover travelled about 7.7 km and worked until 2010, including a winter at 'Husband Hill'.

mars.name: Opportunity (MER-B)
mars.text: Landed on 25 January 2004. Travelled 45.16 km over 14.75 years, until a 2018 dust storm.

mars.name: Phoenix
mars.text: Landed on 25 May 2008. Confirmed water ice in the shallow northern soil and operated through the polar summer.

mars.name: Curiosity (MSL)
mars.text: Landed on 6 August 2012. A car-size rover still exploring Gale crater and the slopes of Aeolis Mons (Mount Sharp).

mars.name: InSight
mars.text: Landed on 26 November 2018. A stationary lander that recorded marsquakes with its seismometer until 2022.

mars.name: Perseverance (Mars 2020)
mars.text: Landed on 18 February 2021 in Jezero crater. Caching samples and carrying the Ingenuity helicopter, which later flew from this site.

mars.name: Tianwen-1 / Zhurong
mars.text: The Zhurong rover was deployed on 14 May 2021 after the Tianwen-1 lander reached Utopia Planitia. It travelled more than 1.9 km.

features.name: Great Red Spot
features.text: A long-lived anticyclonic storm, large enough to hold several Earths. The surface map shows it where Cassini recorded it in December 2000; the spot's longitude drifts over time.

features.name: North-pole hexagon
features.text: A six-sided jet stream around the north pole, recorded in detail by Cassini. The polar close-up used here is a Cassini false-color view so the jet is easier to see.
